segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
to Acre {OCR?: ܠܥܲܟ݁ܘܿ}:
and he brought in with him a multitude of foot soldiers, fighting men, into the city, along with much grain and other necessities.
And he brought the weak out,
and he himself also departed.
And he commanded those inside
that they should not fight only upon the walls,
but should also go outside every day
and attack the Franks,
so that perhaps they might become weakened,
when they were attacked from both sides, by those inside and those outside.
(Now the Franks were so very numerous and powerful
that they were not hindered at all;
only the trouble caused by the city delayed their battle with those outside.
And if it had not been so,
they would quickly have taken it.)
And on the second day (of the week, Monday?), the Frankish horsemen mounted
and approached the tents of the Arabs,
without bringing any foot soldiers with them,
and they caused a great slaughter and returned.
And while the Arabs were pursuing after them,
they took refuge on that hill which is called [the Hill] of the Crosses.
And when Saladin saw that the Franks were helped greatly by the hill,
he decamped and pitched his camp on another hill, opposite the Hill of the Crosses, which overlooks Acre.
And the Arab foot soldiers also used to go out from inside every day,
and fight with the foot soldiers of the Franks.
It is related
that one day the Franks said to the Arabs inside:
"We are tired and weary of the battle of grown men,
and today we wish to amuse ourselves with a battle of little boys."
And they brought about a hundred Frankish boys,
and they brought out from inside a similar number of Arab boys.
And they began to fight by throwing stones,
and then they fought with sticks and staves as they mingled together;
and the Frankish boys put the Arab boys to flight,
and forced them back into the city.
And on the fourth day (of the week, Wednesday?), the twentieth of the seventh month,
there was a fierce battle.
The Franks came out of their tents like locusts.
And the king also went out,
and before him was a Gospel covered with a red satin cloth,
and priests who were carrying it {OCR?: ܠܹܗ} on their shoulders {OCR?: ܟܲܬ݂ܦܵܬ݂ܗܘܿܢ?}.
And when Saladin saw it, he trembled,
and he wailed over his armies and grew fearful. But these Franks {OCR?} kept advancing and growing stronger,
and they were not at all turned back {OCR?} (or: broken {OCR?}?).
